author: Aamaly Hossain
title: Charles commissioners fund $3.4 million for CSM renovation - NewsBreak
text: Roughly $13.7 million in county and state funds will go toward a renovation of two College of Southern Maryland buildings. Charles County commissioners on Tuesday morning unanimously approved using 75% of state funding and a matching 25% of county funding to renovate two of the college's oldest buildings, the campus center and the bookstore, both at the La Plata campus. Bill Comey, vice president of CSM's division of operations and planning, said a portion of the funds will be used for mechanical, electrical and plumbing changes to these buildings, which are over 30-years-old. He said $10.3 million are already in Maryland's budget for the renovation, but the college's board of trustees need county approval to cover the rest of the funds, so the state can see a true commitment to the renovation. The county will be funding roughly $3.4 million, or 25% of the costs, according to the petitioned grant. Commissioner President Reuben B. Collins II (D) said he was glad that the state has adequate funding and is providing a large portion of the project. The fiscal 2027 project will not only renovate the structures but also swap their locations due to a greater demand for a campus center, including student services. The bookstore will move into the current campus center, which is smaller. "When the bookstore was first created, we didn't have online books," Comey said. "We didn't have internet-based learning. So the bookstore is much larger than we need for a bookstore now." The commissioners signed off on the letter of intent, agreeing to support a quarter of the projects finances. Comey said the renovation design will begin in fiscal 2027, and construction is projected to occur in fiscal 2028 and 2029.
